text The most promising construction now has a concrete form. Pairing qubits with similar couplings to a few common noise fields replaces each coupling vector by a difference. Repeating that operation may protect a constant fraction of an unknown register for a polynomially growing time, even when the device has no exact noiseless subspace. I’m checking the whole-register bound, an explicit encoder, and the calibration and control costs before treating this as a physical advantage.

text Compared Markov-control assumptions and conditioned the theorem on the model Estimated required coupling Prepared theorem reference and calibrated control precision The noisy gate calculation passed the key check: errors left some population outside the deep code, but the bound still held without assuming a reset or perfect return. The cost accounting also gives a clear limit. Idle protection improves much faster than the two-body gate budget, and coefficient calibration can dominate both. I’m comparing the same acquired coefficients with conventional outer error correction, which can improve storage further when its recovery cost is supplied.
